clue.text: Massive depletion in solid fuel

indicators.note: in tells us one word goes inside the other here

parts.note: coal is the classic solid fuel
depletion is a loss or running down

explanation.surface: Stocks of coal are running down on a huge scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal: the word for loss splits the fuel word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something enormous in size; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Numbers within the church appear secure

parts.note: C and L are Roman numerals, 100 and 50
within can mean in
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Attendance figures inside a church look safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit side by side: 'within' is not a container signal but simply gives IN. The grid as held prints the last letter as N, a slip for H.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure a deal is to settle it firmly, a common sense of the verb (as in sealing a victory).

clue.text: Novices in the ring take it easy

indicators.note: in places the novices inside the ring here

parts.note: a ring is a loop
L is the learner, a novice driver; two novices give two Ls

explanation.surface: Beginners in a boxing ring decide to go gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. L for a learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display; 'ring' suggests boxing but is just a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to lounge or move in a relaxed, floppy way, so it means to relax.

clue.text: Send rude upsetting letters when separated

indicators.note: upsetting tips the letters of the two words over into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer posts offensive letters after a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting letters' tells us to rearrange SENDRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundered is a literary word for split apart or divided.

clue.text: Caustic article on one particular section of the police

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

parts.words: one particular section of the police
parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece attacks a police department.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid is a corrosive substance, so caustic and acid both mean burning or biting.

clue.text: Saw challenge and took the plunge

parts.note: to vie is to compete or challenge
to take the plunge is an idiom for getting married

explanation.surface: Someone saw a dare and jumped into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took the plunge' looks like diving, but here it is the idiom for marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewed is a past tense meaning looked at, matching the past tense of see.

clue.text: Design for modish nurse

parts.note: modish means fashionable, which is in
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A fashionable new look is proposed for nurses' uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to design to do something and to plan it mean the same.

clue.text: Taking a week-end break, being exhausted

indicators.note: break tells us to break up and rearrange the letters of the words beside it

explanation.surface: Someone takes a weekend off because they are worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' shuffles AWEEKEND; 'Taking' and 'being' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Weakened and exhausted both describe being drained of strength.

clue.text: Cheat the folk present

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating them
a nation is a people or folk

explanation.surface: A con man swindles the people who are in attendance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like an adjective meaning in attendance; it is the noun, a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is a gift, and a gift handed over to a cause is a contribution of that kind.

clue.text: Out of sorts — in love — is in a state!

parts.note: out of sorts means unwell, ill
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lovesick person is in a terrible emotional state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' sounds like agitation, but 'a state' is the definition, a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Air pressure

explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a tune or melody (an air), and strain is also tension or stress.

clue.text: See about the German left when getting on in years

indicators.note: about tells us one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city and see in England
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone visits an old German who has gone off in later life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly means old, advanced in age, a direct synonym.

clue.text: The press wind up ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of means the first piece comes in front of the second

parts.note: to wind up a meeting is to close it

explanation.surface: The newspapers finish a story before the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The press' looks like journalists, but here it is a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is an old word, still used in Scotland and Ireland, for a cupboard, which is a small storage room.

clue.text: Most offensive about the national trust, and most plain-spoken

indicators.note: about shows one word wrapped around another

parts.note: blue means rude or risque, so bluest is most offensive
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Someone attacks the National Trust in the rudest and frankest terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The National Trust looks after historic buildings in Britain; blue humour is smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunt speaker is frank and direct, so the superlative means the most forthright.

clue.text: Apprehends men of the cloth

explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to perceive by intuition; divines are clergymen or theologians.

clue.text: Directions for the cook, not perfectly precise

indicators.note: not perfectly says the word precise is not in its proper order

explanation.surface: Cookbook instructions that are a bit vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not perfectly' reorders PRECISE.
explanation.definitionFit: These are written cooking instructions listing ingredients and method.

clue.text: Refuse a doctor nothing

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A patient turns down a doctor completely.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto something is to forbid or reject it, as to refuse it.

clue.text: MPs score, organising squeeze

indicators.note: organising puts the letters of the words in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament settle a score while setting up a crush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' rearranges MPSSCORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To compress is to press together tightly, a synonym of squeeze.

clue.text: A swimmer in pain and stiffening

indicators.note: in puts the swimmer inside the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
an eel is a swimming fish

explanation.surface: A fish in agony goes rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'A swimmer' suggests a person but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeling oneself is hardening one's resolve, a figurative strengthening.

clue.text: Rather tame show cracked up

indicators.note: cracked up suggests something broken apart and reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A dull performance has been overhyped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked up' rearranges TAMESHOW; it looks like praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat and rather both mean to some degree, fairly.

clue.text: Curse a little having a go at house repairs

indicators.note: a little of the following words means a short run of letters taken from inside them

parts.words: having a go at house repairs

explanation.surface: A DIY enthusiast swears while having a go at fixing the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' picks the run across 'go at house'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a swear word, a profanity uttered in anger.

clue.text: Greek character holding cross on back seat

indicators.note: holding shows the Greek letter wrapping round the word for cross

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ill can mean bad-tempered or hostile, as in ill humour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek holding a crucifix rides on the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal; 'cross' looks like a crucifix but means bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillion is the passenger seat behind the rider on a motorcycle or horse.

clue.text: Notorious criminal — top one

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gangster is described as the leading one.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was a famous American gangster, an example of an infamous lawbreaker.

clue.text: Everyone out to make a hit

explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a walkout by all the workers; to strike is to hit or score a success.

clue.text: Just say he's an old-fashioned craftsman

indicators.note: say tells us the word is said out loud

parts.note: just means fair, which is right

explanation.surface: Someone simply claims to be a traditional artisan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' sounds like an adverb meaning simply, but it is an adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A wright is an archaic word for a maker or builder, kept in shipwright and wheelwright.

clue.text: Bishops making report in addition to writing

indicators.note: in shows the word for report placed inside the other piece

parts.note: PS is a postscript, an addition to a letter
to relate is to report or tell

explanation.surface: Church leaders produce a report alongside their written work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'making' is a link word. A postscript is added to the end of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prelates are senior clergy such as bishops or archbishops.

clue.text: Superior punter

explanation.definitionFit: Better means of higher quality; a bettor or better is someone who places wagers.

clue.text: Fair penalty

explanation.definitionFit: Fine weather is fair weather; a fine is a monetary penalty.

clue.text: There's no team backing for an inventor

indicators.note: backing means the words before it are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a side is a team

explanation.surface: No team is willing to support an inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses NOSIDE as a whole. Thomas Edison invented the phonograph and electric light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison is a famous American inventor, an example of the type.

clue.text: Frivolous in a note, but illuminating

parts.note: light means frivolous, not serious
taken as written
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Light-hearted in tone but informative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'illuminating' seems to mean informative, but it is literal: giving light.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting a room is illuminating it; both describe making something bright.

clue.text: A little seal gets in — gets put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A seal pup gets inside, then is thrown out again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges GETSIN; the seal is not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a small seal, often set into a ring, used to mark documents.

clue.text: People in singlet, casual shirt, or formal wear

indicators.note: in shows the people placed inside the pieces for the garments

parts.note: a vest is a singlet, a sleeveless undershirt in British usage
a T-shirt gives T
men are people

explanation.surface: Folk dressed in vests, T-shirts or something smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal, with the people between the two garments. In Britain a vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial robe, especially one worn by clergy.
